papers.title: Which Voices Move Markets? Speaker Identity and the Cross-Section of Post-Earnings Returns
papers.summary: 16,428 S&P 500 earnings calls (2015-2025), 6.5M sentences analyzed with FinBERT segmented by speaker role. Speaker-weighted sentiment (Analyst 49%, CFO 30%, Exec 16%, Other 5%) → OOS Spearman IC=0.142, monthly long-short alpha=2.03% (t=6.49) vs FF5. Subsumes LM dictionary entirely (LM t=0.86 vs FinBERT t=5.90). Soft information sluggishly incorporated.
papers.relevance_reason: Directly upgrades H163 design: use speaker-weighted FinBERT instead of flat average. Provides exact weights and performance metrics.

papers.title: Cross-Stock Predictability via LLM-Augmented Semantic Networks
papers.summary: Two-stage pairs trading: (1) sparse candidate graph from 10-K sentence-BERT embeddings, (2) LLM filters edges by economic relation quality. S&P 500 2011-2019: Sharpe 0.742→0.820, MaxDD -10.47%→-7.85%. Shows LLM can replace ad-hoc pair selection with principled semantic filtering.
papers.relevance_reason: Directly improves H160 (factor-residualized pairs) by replacing manual pair curation with LLM-filtered semantic network. Blocked on H160 confirming first.

papers.title: Can LLM-based Financial Investing Strategies Outperform the Market in Long Run?
papers.summary: FINSABER framework: 20 years, 100+ symbols. Conclusion: LLM timing strategies do NOT outperform passive benchmarks long-run. Overly conservative in bull markets, overly aggressive in bear markets. Recommendation: use for trend detection + regime-aware risk controls only.
papers.relevance_reason: Critical caution for H165 (TradingAgents): don't use as standalone market timer. Design note to restrict to regime gate role. Low-risk wiki update.

papers.title: Extracting the Structure of Press Releases for Predicting Earnings Announcement Returns
papers.summary: 138k+ earnings press releases (2005-2023). Soft info (text) as informative as EPS surprise. FinBERT best performer. BUT: stock prices fully incorporate press release info at market open — limits exploitability unless real-time pre-open access achieved.
papers.relevance_reason: Validates FinBERT for press release analysis but caution: prices already reflect info at open. Confirms H163 is chasing a tight window. Not staging separately — already covered by H163 design.

papers.title: Lumibot — backtesting + live trading framework
papers.summary: Algorithmic trading framework where same code runs for backtesting and live trading. Supports stocks, options, crypto, futures, forex. Multiple brokers. ~4k stars.
papers.relevance_reason: Useful if we want a unified backtest+live framework. Currently we use yfinance+custom for backtest, Alpaca for live. Low priority given current stack works.
